title: Tenant location proof assembler and audit bundle exporter for dedicated capacity
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an automated service that collects, signs, packages, and exports tenant isolation evidence for Dedicated capacity customers. The service (proof-assembler) must gather deterministic artifacts that demonstrate where tenant workloads ran, their tenancy boundaries, and retention metadata. Output will be a tamper-evident audit bundle consumable by auditors and by Redwood's Compliance team.
acceptance_criteria: Proof assembler collects a configurable minimal artifact set for a tenant: node assignment records, container/pod metadata (image id, container id), host-zone geotag, orchestration allocation snapshot (timestamped), and network isolation assertions.
Each artifact is timestamped and signed with the tenant-evidence signing key stored in HSM/KMS; signature metadata included in bundle manifest.
Bundles are exportable via an authenticated API (GET /v1/tenants/{id}/evidence?from=...&to=...) and as scheduled exports to a customer S3/GCS location with retention labels.
Generated bundles include a human-readable summary (PDF) and machine-verifiable manifest (JSON) with checksums; manifest fields documented in the spec.
Bundle generation supports GDPR/localization flags to redact PII when requested by the tenant and logs redaction decisions.

End-to-end test: create synthetic tenant on dedicated pool in eu-west, trigger export for a 24h window, verify signature chain, verify manifest checksums, and confirm the bundle is parsable by the compliance verification tool.
Operational: production alerts for export failures, signing errors, or missing artifact types; retry policy defined and implemented.
Documentation: Confluence spec, API docs, and a runbook for on-call engineers and customer success to deliver bundles to auditors.
technical_notes: Artifact sources: node-manager (allocations), kube-controller (pod snapshots), tenant-network-proxy (flow labels), host-metadata-service (zone/geolocation), storage-retention-service (policy flags), and auditd logs for relevant hosts.

Signing model: use KMS asymmetric keys with sigstore-style transparency metadata; include public key and key-id in manifest. Consider timestamping via a coordinator that queries NTP and signs timestamp to mitigate drift.
Storage: temporary staging in encrypted blob store with strict TTL before moving to customer export bucket; use envelope encryption with per-customer data key.
Formats: artifacts stored as gzipped newline-delimited JSON, with SHA256 checksums recorded in manifest. PDF summary generated from template populated by manifest fields.
Performance: bundle generation for 24h window for medium tenant (<=100k requests/day) must complete within 15 minutes; implement sharded collector jobs per node to parallelize.
Tamper evidence: manifest includes per-file checksum, signed manifest, and an optional merkle root for all file checksums to allow compact verification.
RBAC: only authorized SRE/compliance roles can request historical bundles; API uses mTLS for server-to-server exports and short-lived signed export tokens for customer S3 destinations.
Failure modes: partial artifact collection allowed if manifest flags missing artifacts; bundle must indicate confidence level (complete | partial | degraded) and list missing artifacts.
Data minimization: default bundle excludes process-level traces and user payloads; an escalation workflow exists for auditors to request expanded artifacts under DPA with legal sign-off.
Backwards compatibility: design export manifest v1 with explicit version field to allow future schema changes without breaking verifier tools.
Observability: add per-export metrics (duration_seconds, files_count, signed_ok, export_status) and tracing for each collector step.
rollout_plan: 1) Build prototype collector and signer in staging wired to a single dedicated pool (feature-flagged).
2) Run two-week smoke with internal compliance and a pilot customer, collect feedback and iterate manifest schema.
3) Security review and key ceremony to onboard KMS signing key into production.
4) Enable scheduled exports (daily/weekly) for Tiered Dedicated customers and expose API for on-demand exports.
5) Monitor errors and performance for 30 days, iterate on retries and resource limits, then flip default to GA for Dedicated tier.
dependencies: ENG-89911 (kms-integration: asymmetric signing and key rotation)
SEC-310 (legal: DPA amendment for auditor artifact access)
comments: 2025-11-12 Asha Patel: Created ticket after legal requested a standardized artifact bundle for Dedicated customers undergoing audits. Initial scope captures node assignment, container ids, host geo, and orchestration snapshots.

2025-11-20 Liam Navarro: Spike complete — prototype collector can fetch allocation history and build manifest. Observed clock skew between node-manager and kube-controller; adding NTP-timestamp step to signer.

2025-11-27 Security review kickoff: SEC assigned to consult on KMS key ceremony and whether to store public keys in an external transparency log. Risk: customer may request signatures with customer-provided key — policy TBD.

2025-12-01 QA: End-to-end test with synthetic tenant in eu-west shows bundle generation 12 minutes for 24h window; PDF summary had truncated pod image names — fixed template to include full image digest.

2025-12-03 PM sync: Added scheduled export feature and S3 delivery config to acceptance criteria; decided to include redaction flag to hide PII by default. Liam to prepare Confluence runbook for CS handoff.
